title: TrailGuard AI cameras in the Kanha-Pench corridor transmit tiger alerts to researchers and forest officials 30 to 42 seconds after detection in a 2022 pilot
summary: TrailGuard AI cameras sent tiger alerts to researchers and forest officials within 30 to 42 seconds, and officials later warned village leaders by text chat, though not rapidly.
account: Dertien et al. reported in BioScience (published 14 September 2023) that 12 TrailGuard AI camera-alert systems ran in the Kanha-Pench corridor, Madhya Pradesh. They ran from mid-May to mid-July 2022 (591 trap nights). The cameras run embedded AI on an Intel Myriad chip to detect tigers and humans and transmit only images of interest. Researchers and forest department officials received tiger notifications 30 to 42 seconds after detection. The authors report that forest officials sent text-chat warnings to village leaders after detections that concerned them, although these messages were not rapid. They also report that the sample was too small to determine an effect on human–wildlife conflict. The paper's second site, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in Uttar Pradesh, where a unit captured armed poachers, is recorded separately. The Hindu (16 September 2023) reported the Madhya Pradesh deployment. It quoted H.S. Negi of the Global Tiger Forum on plans to incorporate the system in other tiger reserves. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim that the cameras were “immediately effective, picking up a tiger just 300 meters from a village”. No forest department document on the pilot is among the sources.
purpose: Real-time detection of tigers and humans for human-wildlife conflict early warning and anti-poaching. The reported detections and follow-up were the intended use.
system: TrailGuard AI camera-alert system with embedded AI (Intel Myriad processor; detectors trained with CVEDIA synthetic renderings)
developer: RESOLVE (design) with CVEDIA Ltd (AI training); units manufactured by Nightjar
deployer: Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh forest departments with Clemson University, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum
segment: State forest departments and conservation research partners

They also report that the sample was too small to determine an effect on human–wildlife conflict. The paper's second site, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in Uttar Pradesh, where a unit captured armed poachers, is recorded separately. The Hindu (16 September 2023) reported the Madhya Pradesh deployment. It quoted H.S. Negi of the Global Tiger Forum on plans to incorporate the system in other tiger reserves. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim that the cameras were “immediately effective, picking up a tiger just 300 meters from a village”. No forest department document on the pilot is among the sources.
